special 30th Anniversary Limited Edition created for the Japanese domestic market to commemorate 30 years of Mazda rotary-engine production. Production of the Type RS-R was limited to just 500 examples for Japan, making it a particularly distinctive factory variant of the FD-generation RX-7. The anniversary specification combined the Type RS platform with exclusive Sunburst Yellow paint, special gunmetal-finished wheels, Bilstein dampers derived from the Type RZ, and unique RS-R-specific details.At the heart of the RS-R is Mazda's legendary 13B-REW sequential twin-turbo rotary engine paired with a 5-speed manual transmission and rear-wheel drive. The lightweight FD chassis utilizes double-wishbone independent suspension, four-wheel ventilated disc brakes, and power-assisted rack-and-pinion steering, while the RS-R's factory Bilstein dampers provide additional performance-focused chassis hardware. This example retains the right-hand-drive configuration appropriate to its Japanese-market origins.The anniversary-specific interior incorporates details unique to the RS-R, including an RS-R-specific instrument paneltreatment, chrome-plated gauge rings, and a fine-scale speedometer and tachometer.Performance has been enhanced with a period-appropriate collection of Japanese components centered around an ARC front-mount intercooler with GReddy intercooler piping and an AutoExe Style cold air intake. An HKS Ti Hi-Power cat-back exhaust complements the upgraded intake and charge-air system while adding the distinctive exhaust character associated with a modified 13B-REW rotary.The chassis has been upgraded with Fortune Auto 500 Series coilovers, an AutoExe front strut tower bar, and a Cusco rear strut bar, providing adjustable suspension and additional chassis reinforcement. A Chase Bays brake booster delete kit further contributes to the performance-focused configuration, while 18-inch Work Emotion XD9 wheels finished in Grey with Muteki lug nuts provide a classic Japanese motorsport-inspired fitment.The exterior Driver monitoring has been comprehensively upgraded with a Defi-Link Control Unit II controlling individual Defi boost, oil-temperature, and water-temperature gauges. A custom 3D-printed dual gauge pod and steering-wheel gauge pod integrate the additional instrumentation into the right-hand-drive cockpit, providing important real-time information for the modified twin-turbo rotary powertrain.Inside, a MOMO Race steering wheel provides a more direct driver interface, while a carbon fiber shift knob, carbon fiber door sill trim plates, RHD passenger footrest, and custom 3D-printed cup holder add further enthusiast-focused details. The audio system has also been modernized with a Kenwood double-DIN head unit, Kicker Comp 12-inch subwoofer and enclosure, Kicker CXA300.1 amplifier, and Focal tweeters with a Focal Access passive crossover network.With nearly $40,000 invested, this RX-7 Type RS-R combines the rarity and historical significance of Mazda's 500-unit 30th Anniversary specification with an extensive collection of period-inspired Japanese performance and styling components from ARC, HKS, GReddy, AutoExe, Cusco, Defi, Ganador, Work Emotion, and MOMO. description: 1999 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 Z71 4x4 â€ Regular Cab, Vortec 5.3 V8, Black on Black Why This Car Is Special The 1999 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 Z71 represents something that is genuinely hard to find today: the first model year of a generation that truck enthusiasts have spent the better part of two decades hunting down in clean, original condition. Chevrolet debuted the GMT800 platform for 1999, replacing the long-running C/K series with a truck that was wider, quieter, and more refined without abandoning the body-on-frame, V8-powered formula that made the nameplate dominant. The Silverado name itself was new for 1999, elevated from trim level to model designation as GM reorganized its full-size truck lineup. This particular truck is a 1999 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 Z71 in regular cab configuration, finished in black over a black leather interior. The Z71 Off-Road Package was one of the most popular option packages Chevrolet offered on the Silverado at the time, adding an off-road-tuned suspension, Bilstein-style shock absorbers, transfer case skid plates, and the automatic four-wheel drive system that let the driver select between 2Hi, Auto 4WD, 4Hi, and 4Lo from a dashboard-mounted switch. What makes this truck especially interesting from a collector's standpoint is the regular cab body combined with the Z71 package â€ a combination that gives you genuine off-road hardware in the simplest, cleanest body style the 1500 was offered in. The VIN confirms this is a 1500 series half-ton (not a 2500 or 3500), built with the Vortec 5.3L V8, and assembled at a GM truck plant. The 5.3 was the engine of choice for Z71 buyers who wanted meaningful towing capacity â€ rated at approximately 7,000 pounds in properly equipped 1999 configurations â€ with the kind of low-end torque that made the Vortec family so well regarded. This engine architecture went on to serve as the foundation for GM's LS-based small block development well into the 2000s, and the 5.3 in particular became one of the most sought-after swap engines in the enthusiast community because of its combination of displacement, efficiency, and durability. First-year GMT800 trucks like this 1999 Silverado are now firmly in collectible territory. Finding one in regular cab form, with the Z71 package intact, leather interior, and the blacked-out appearance this truck presents, is increasingly uncommon. Most 1999 Silverados that have survived in decent shape have been worked hard. This one presents as a truck that has been kept up rather than used up. description: 1987 Chevrolet K5 Blazer Silverado â€ Black on Red, 350 V8, Clean Frame Why This Car Is Special The 1987 Chevrolet K5 Blazer Silverado occupies a specific place in American truck history that is increasingly difficult to explain to anyone who didn't live through it. This was the last full decade of the original full-size Blazer format â€ a body-on-frame, two-door, removable-hardtop SUV built on the same K10 half-ton 4x4 platform as the C/K pickup trucks. Chevrolet introduced the K5 Blazer for the 1969 model year as a direct answer to the Ford Bronco, and by the time this 1987 example was built, the formula had been refined over nearly two decades into something genuinely capable and comfortable at the same time. The third-generation body style, known internally as the GMT400 predecessor or the 'square body,' actually ran from 1973 through 1991 for the full-size Blazer. By 1987, Chevrolet had been refining this platform for fourteen years. The result was a truck that felt mature â€ solid doors, tight body gaps, a well-thought-out interior layout, and enough powertrain options to satisfy buyers ranging from weekend campers to serious off-road users. What makes this particular 1987 Chevrolet K5 Blazer Silverado worth paying attention to is the combination of trim level, powertrain, condition, and color. The Silverado package was the top trim offered on the K5 Blazer, placing it above the base and Custom Deluxe configurations. It brought a higher level of interior finish, additional chrome exterior detailing, and the Silverado badge on the dash and instrument panel. The black exterior over a full red cloth interior is a striking factory combination, and the underside photos confirm what collectors are always hoping to see: a clean, solid frame with no significant rust or structural concerns. For a nearly forty-year-old truck, that detail matters more than almost anything else. The VIN on this truck confirms it is a genuine K-series (four-wheel-drive) half-ton Blazer, built in Flint, Michigan, for the 1987 model year, with the 5.7-liter V8 engine. This is not a two-wheel-drive model rebadged, and it is not a later GMT400-generation truck. It is exactly what it presents itself as. In 1987, this engine was carbureted and produced approximately 210 horsepower and 300 lb-ft of torque in its standard K5 Blazer tune. It backs up to a 4-speed automatic transmission, which in this application would be the TH700-R4 (also called the 4L60), an overdrive-equipped unit that Chevrolet introduced in 1982 to improve highway fuel economy without sacrificing the 350's low-end torque characteristics. The overdrive fourth gear made a meaningful difference on long highway drives compared to the earlier TH350 three-speed that had powered earlier K5 Blazers. description: 1988 Chevrolet C-1500 Silverado â€ Long Bed Fleetside with 350 V8 and Clean Undercarriage Why This Car Is Special The 1988 Chevrolet C-1500 Silverado represents the final generation of what collectors now call the 'Square Body' or 'OBS' â€ the third-generation C/K trucks that ran from 1973 through 1987, with a mild refresh that carried the design into 1991. That generation is widely regarded as the last truly simple, body-on-frame, no-frills full-size truck Chevrolet built before cab-forward aerodynamics and increasing computer complexity changed the formula permanently. The square body trucks have been climbing steadily in collector value, and the Silverado trim level has always been the one worth finding. By 1988, Chevrolet had updated the front end with a more refined grille and fascia compared to the earlier square body trucks, and the interior had been substantially modernized. This particular truck â€ a two-wheel-drive long bed regular cab â€ is the configuration most commonly associated with the workhorse American pickup of its era. It was spec'd with the Silverado trim package, the top-of-the-line designation for the C/K line at that time, which meant a notably higher level of comfort and chrome than the base Custom or Scottsdale trucks below it. The Silverado package brought upgraded cloth upholstery, additional sound deadening, chrome interior trim accents, and the door panel badging visible in the photos. It was the truck that Chevrolet was positioning against the Ford F-150 XLT Lariat, and it held its own. The truck is finished in red with a matching red interior â€ a color combination that was popular in the late 1980s and reads as very intentional on a truck this age. Both the exterior and the interior have held up with the kind of consistency that suggests this truck was either lightly used or carefully kept. The undercarriage photos confirm the latter: the frame, floor pans, and structural areas beneath this truck are clean and solid, which is the single most important thing to verify on any truck from this era. Throttle Body Injection, or TBI, uses two injectors mounted in a throttle body that looks visually similar to a carburetor but delivers fuel with greater consistency and cold-start reliability. It is one of the most straightforward fuel injection systems ever put into production, which is a significant advantage from a long-term ownership standpoint: TBI systems are easy to diagnose, well-supported by aftermarket parts, and fully compatible with standard mechanical skills. The 350 in this application produced around 210 horsepower when new, which in a truck of this weight class translates to confident, linear power delivery. Backing the 350 is the 700R4 four-speed overdrive automatic transmission, introduced by GM in 1982 to bring highway fuel economy to trucks that were previously running three-speed automatics with no overdrive ratio. The fourth gear overdrive ratio reduces engine RPM at highway speeds, which eases mechanical wear and noticeably improves fuel consumption on the open road. description: This 2024 Honda Odyssey Elite in white represents the pinnacle of family transportation, offering refined comfort and capability for your daily journeys. With 49,933 miles, this minivan has been carefully maintained and is ready to serve your family's needs for years to come.  - 3.5L V6 SOHC i-VTEC 24V engine with 10-speed automatic transmission - 500-Watt AM/FM/HD Premium Audio System with 11 speakers - Honda Satellite-Linked Navigation System - Apple CarPlay and Android Auto integration - Adaptive Cruise Control with Low-Speed Follow - Lane Keeping Assist System with active safety monitoring - Blind Spot Information System with visual warnings - Power liftgate for convenient cargo access - Heated leather front seats with memory function - Power moonroof - Auto-dimming rear-view mirror and heated door mirrors - Exterior rear parking camera - 19-inch machine-finished alloy wheels  The Elite trim delivers premium comfort features that make every drive enjoyable. Dual-zone automatic climate control keeps front and rear passengers comfortable, while the heated steering wheel and heated front seats provide warmth during colder months. The power driver seat with memory settings allows you to find your ideal driving position instantly. Three rows of seating accommodate up to eight passengers, with a split-folding rear seat and reclining third-row seats for maximum flexibility in how you arrange your space and cargo.  Safety is paramount in this Odyssey, which includes electronic stability control, four-wheel independent suspension, and multiple airbags strategically positioned throughout the cabin. Lane Keeping Assist helps keep you centered in your lane, while Blind Spot Information System alerts you to vehicles in your blind spots. The adaptive cruise control system maintains a safe following distance in traffic, reducing driver fatigue on longer commutes.  Technology seamlessly integrates into your daily routine with Honda Satellite-Linked Navigation that keeps you on course, SiriusXM satellite radio for entertainment options, and CabinControl for managing your vehicle remotely. The power moonroof adds natural light and an open-air feel, while exterior parking camera assistance makes maneuvering tight spaces straightforward.  This Odyssey achieves an estimated 19 city and 28 highway mpg, providing practical fuel economy for a vehicle in this class. The 10-speed automatic transmission delivers smooth acceleration and efficient cruising, while all-wheel independent suspension ensures a composed ride whether you're navigating city streets or highway stretches. description: Supercharged V6 power. quattro all-wheel drive. Three-row versatility. Bose audio. Virtual Cockpit. And an equipment list that reads more like a flagship luxury SUV than a typical used crossover. This 2018 Audi Q7 3.0T Premium Plus quattro is loaded with the options that make this generation of Q7 so desirable.  Finished in Glacier White Metallic over Black leather, this Q7 combines understated Audi design with serious capability and a cabin built for long-distance comfort.  Under the hood is Audi's 3.0-liter supercharged TFSI V6 paired with an 8-speed Tiptronic automatic transmission and quattro all-wheel drive.  The supercharged V6 is a major part of this Q7's appeal. Its smooth, immediate power delivery gives this three-row SUV the effortless character you'd expect from a premium European vehicle, while quattro provides additional confidence through wet Northwest weather, winter driving, and trips across the mountain passes.  This particular Q7 goes considerably beyond the basics.  Audi Virtual Cockpit replaces the traditional gauge cluster with Audi's configurable digital display, while MMI Navigation Plus with MMI Touch brings navigation and infotainment into the center of the experience. Audi Smartphone Interface adds modern phone connectivity, and the 3D Bose Surround Sound system transforms the cabin with a substantial premium-audio upgrade.  Comfort is equally impressive.  Leather seating, heated and ventilated front seats, heated rear seats, four-zone automatic climate control, memory seating, a power-adjustable steering column with memory, power-folding heated mirrors, rear window shades, and a panoramic moonroof make this Q7 exceptionally well equipped for both driver and passengers.  And unlike many luxury SUVs, there's genuine family versatility behind the premium materials.  A third-row bench provides additional passenger capacity when needed, while the power liftgate makes the cargo area easy to access. The Warm Weather and Cold Weather Packages help prepare the cabin for both ends of the Northwest climate.  The Vision Package adds another layer of technology with Audi Virtual Cockpit, full LED lighting, and a Topview Camera System that provides a much better perspective when maneuvering a vehicle of this size. Audi Side Assist with Pre Sense Rear adds useful driver-awareness technology on the highway.  This Q7 is also equipped for more than commuting.  The factory Towing Package and 7-pin connector give it additional utility for someone who wants to bring along a trailer or other recreational equipment, making the combination of V6 power, quattro AWD, three-row seating, and towing hardware particularly useful for an active Northwest lifestyle.  With 105,953 miles, we're not trying to sell this as a low-mileage luxury SUV. We're selling what it actually is: a two-owner, accident-free Q7 with an exceptional equipment list and the drivetrain buyers specifically seek out in this generation.  Premium Plus Package. Vision Package. Cold Weather Package. Warm Weather Package. Towing Package. Virtual Cockpit. Bose 3D audio. Heated and ventilated front seats. Heated rear seats. Four-zone climate control. Topview cameras. Three rows. Supercharged V6. quattro.  That's a lot of Audi for the money.  Offered by Honda of Kirkland, backed by more than 30 years of serving the greater Seattle and Kirkland communities.  If you're shopping for a premium three-row SUV and care more about drivetrain, equipment, history, and value than simply finding the lowest number on an odometer, come see this Q7 in person. The supercharged V6 and quattro get your attention, but the accident-free history and unusually deep option list are what make this Glacier White Premium Plus worth a closer look.[!@@Additional
